clue.text: You can't go through the card if you stick to these courses

definitions.text: You can't go through the card if you stick to these courses

parts.words: You can't go through the card if you stick to these courses
parts.note: the card is the restaurant's à la carte menu; a fixed-price set meal of several courses means no ranging over it, while the surface hints at golf or racing courses

explanation.surface: A golfer or racegoer who sticks to certain courses can never get through the whole card.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed menu of set courses at a set price is the opposite of choosing freely from the card.

clue.text: One may be seen hanging around a low joint

definitions.text: One may be seen hanging around a low joint

parts.words: One may be seen hanging around a low joint
parts.note: a low joint sounds like a seedy bar, but it is the lowest joint of the leg, and the thing hanging round it is a piece of jewellery

explanation.surface: Someone loitering outside a disreputable bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain or bangle worn round the joint just above the foot is this ornament.

clue.text: Periodical heed-taker

definitions.meaning: one who pays attention to what is said

explanation.surface: A magazine that pays attention.
explanation.definitionFit: The Listener was a long-running British weekly, and someone who hears and takes notice is literally one who listens.

clue.text: Fly from Polish road accident

indicators.note: an accident wrecks things, so the letters of the two words are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A fly emerges from a road crash in Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accident' turns POLISH ROAD into the fruit-fly genus; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the genus of small fruit flies used widely in genetics research.

clue.text: Order new-style silk for memorial

parts.note: the OBE is the Order of the British Empire, an honour

indicators.note: giving the silk a new style means rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: Commanding that silk be made in a fresh fashion for a memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a command but is the honour; 'new-style' rearranges the silk; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall tapering stone pillar is often raised as a monument to the dead.

clue.text: Whirl round Mary Baker

definitions.meaning: to swirl in a small circular current
Mary Baker ... founded the Christian Science movement

explanation.surface: A woman named Mary Baker spinning about.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that swirls in circles does this, and the founder of Christian Science bore this surname.

clue.text: The less welcome of Kipling's impostors

definitions.text: The less welcome of Kipling's impostors

parts.words: The less welcome of Kipling's impostors
parts.note: Kipling's poem If speaks of meeting Triumph and its opposite and treating 'those two impostors just the same'; the unwelcome one is the calamity

explanation.surface: Picking the less pleasant of two frauds in a Kipling story.
explanation.definitionFit: In If, Triumph is paired with catastrophe, and catastrophe is clearly the less welcome of the pair.

clue.text: So address 13 on stationery?

parts.note: entry 13 is defined as a man of letters, so the head of the letters is a playful title for him, while really it is the printed heading on notepaper

explanation.surface: Writing the address of a postal official on notepaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed name and address at the top of writing paper is its heading, a pun on the chief of letters.

clue.text: A suitable -case for referring to the Receiver

definitions.text: A suitable -case for referring to the Receiver

parts.words: A suitable -case for referring to the Receiver
parts.note: the Receiver looks like an official receiver in bankruptcy, but in grammar the case of the indirect object, the one who receives, is meant

explanation.surface: A bankruptcy case that ought to be sent to the Official Receiver.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the case marking the recipient of something given is the indirect-object case.

clue.text: Like sops well stirred — the nursery sort perhaps

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Like bread soaked in milk and stirred, the nursery sort of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well stirred' rearranges LIKESOPS; sops suggests nursery food, but the nursery is a beginners' slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle beginners' run on a mountain is called the nursery slope.

clue.text: Helps you change, but not into clerical gear

definitions.text: Helps you change, but not into clerical gear

parts.words: Helps you change, but not into clerical gear
parts.note: not clerical means lay, and the change is of gear in a gearbox, not a change of clothes into a cassock

explanation.surface: Someone who assists you in changing clothes, though not into a priest's vestments.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary shaft in a gearbox carries the gears that make changing between ratios possible.

clue.text: Knocked back in cricket practice, this shooter

indicators.note: knocked back means reversed, so the word for the practice area is read right to left

parts.note: cricketers practise in the nets

explanation.surface: A gun knocked back during a cricket net session.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sten gun was a British submachine gun of the Second World War.

clue.text: Crooked shyster, apt to make Scots hop

indicators.note: crooked suggests a dishonest lawyer, but here it twists the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A dishonest lawyer is likely to set the Scots dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooked' rearranges SHYSTERAPT; 'to make' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A strathspey is a slow Scottish country dance, so a Highland hop of sorts.

clue.text: Scholar of Merton, obviously a man of letters

definitions.meaning: scholarship holders at Merton College, Oxford, are given this special title
jokingly, the official in charge of a post office deals in letters

explanation.surface: An Oxford scholar who is plainly literary.
explanation.definitionFit: Merton College calls its scholars by this name, and the head of a post office handles mail all day.

clue.text: Italian (of course) thick but full of beans

definitions.text: Italian (of course) thick but full of beans

parts.words: Italian (of course) thick but full of beans
parts.note: thick and full of beans sound like dim but lively, of a person, but the Italian is a dish served as a course: a hearty soup with beans and vegetables

explanation.surface: An Italian who is stupid yet energetic.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a thick Italian vegetable soup often containing beans and pasta, served as a first course.

clue.text: Don't do it — it's a burden

definitions.meaning: to hold back from an action
a burden is the chorus repeated in a song

explanation.surface: Advice to abstain because it is a heavy load.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to hold back from acting, and in old usage a song's burden is its repeated chorus.

clue.text: Strangely prescient about what L drivers may do on holiday

indicators.note: about means one word goes around another

parts.note: fey means having uncanny second sight
learner drivers (shown by L plates) often let the engine cut out

explanation.surface: An oddly far-sighted person describes learner drivers' antics while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: L plates mark learner drivers in Britain; 'about' signals the container. Fey usually means otherworldly, and 'Strangely' adds that uncanny flavour to prescient.
explanation.definitionFit: Festal means belonging to a feast or holiday, so the adverb describes doing something in festive style.

clue.text: Write on the back the place of which we hear directions?

parts.words: the place of which we hear
parts.note: Endor is the biblical place of the famous Witch; 'of which we hear' puns on which and witch
S and E are south and east, two compass points

explanation.surface: A request to note on the reverse the location we are told about.
explanation.walkthrough: The Witch of Endor appears in the first book of Samuel; 'we hear' only signals the which-witch pun, so no sound-alike is entered.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign or write on the reverse of a cheque is the original sense of this verb.

clue.text: Is Bondi a formation of volcanic rock?

indicators.note: a formation is an arrangement, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A question whether Sydney's Bondi Beach is formed of lava.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formation of' rearranges ISBONDIA; formation also tempts as a geological word.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsidian is a dark natural glass formed when lava cools very fast.

clue.text: Sounds a suitable bird on the menu

indicators.note: sounds means the next word is heard, not spelt, so another word of the same sound is entered

parts.note: meet is an old word for suitable or fitting
pie is an old name for the magpie

explanation.surface: Noises from a fitting bird served at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastry case filled with meat is a staple dish found on menus.

clue.text: Maybe steep parts of these to check, eg, acidity

indicators.note: maybe signals that the words could be rearranged into these, a reverse anagram in effect

explanation.surface: Steep parts of something tested for acidity.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says steep parts may be an anagram of these; 'of these' points back to the answer. Litmus papers are the classic check.
explanation.definitionFit: Strips of litmus or indicator paper are dipped in liquids to show acidity or alkalinity.

clue.text: Betrayed, especially when down river

definitions.meaning: the idiom ... down the river means betrayed

explanation.surface: Treachery, especially downstream.
explanation.definitionFit: To be betrayed is to be handed over for gain, most famously in the idiom about the river.

clue.text: Some crumpet, often toasted

parts.note: crumpet is a tea-time cake you toast, but also old British slang for attractive women; at dinners a toast is drunk to the women present

explanation.surface: A crumpet frequently put under the grill.
explanation.definitionFit: Women collectively, toasted at formal dinners, were slangily called crumpet in Britain.

clue.text: Resolute chap to drag army of women back

indicators.note: back means the run of pieces is read from right to left

parts.note: to trawl is to drag a net
the ATS was the Auxiliary Territorial Service, the British women's army of the Second World War

explanation.surface: A determined man hauls a women's army corps backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TRAWLATS into the answer; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A loyal and dependable supporter is called a stalwart, a firm and steadfast person.

clue.text: Smart lad wanted

parts.note: reads like a job advert, but asks for the boy's name that follows 'smart' in the phrase for a know-all

explanation.surface: A job advert seeking a bright young man.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart alec is a cocky know-all, so this is the lad's name the phrase wants.

clue.text: This sums up those who multiply quickly

definitions.text: This sums up those who multiply quickly

parts.words: This sums up those who multiply quickly
parts.note: sums and multiply suggest a fast mental arithmetician, but multiply means breed, and the word describes creatures that reproduce fast

explanation.surface: A word for people who are quick at multiplication.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals or plants that produce many offspring readily are described as fruitful in this sense.

clue.text: Been lacerated a bit by corset?

indicators.note: a bit of the phrase means some consecutive letters inside it are taken

explanation.surface: Was someone cut by a tight corset?
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit' takes letters from bEEN LACErated; corset is a verb here; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To corset is to lace tightly round, and this verb means to bind or wrap with laces.

clue.text: Conservative Bar head has ingenuity

parts.note: a lever is a bar used to prise
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: A Tory leader of the Bar shows ingenuity.
explanation.walkthrough: Bar and head look like the legal profession and its leader; they are a lever and a headland; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingenuity and smartness are synonyms for quick inventive intelligence.
